title: bug: a verified-local worker or QA job cannot run the project's tests: the agent job's PATH (guest-supervisor.py JOB_PATH) leaves out the pinned Node toolchain, so node/npm are "not found" (exit 127) in the seat VM
description:
Found by the governor's DoD 8 Windows real-VM run for task-1a8f1d0e on 2026-11-06, with plugin 15c7fb34 (zip sha256 74520ab6…) in scratch project C:\moe-scratch\vl-e2e on task-7a9ae68a ("mul helper").
The VM route worked:
- `[seat] started moe-vm-8390b245f00d796ef0da`
- `[seat] VM credential account=acct-2 source=signin`
- `[seat] job role=worker …`
- `[OK] MOE_VM_CANDIDATE_COMMITTED … paths=2`
- `[seat] stopped …`
But the agent reported: "there is no `node` or `npm` in this workspace, so I could not run the red or green steps. The command exited 127 (not found)." It started step 1, completed no step, and its complete_task was refused. The task went back to WORKING.

Cause, in scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py:
- :910 sets JOB_PATH = '/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin'.
- :1017 builds the agent job env with 'PATH': JOB_PATH.
- :911 says TOOLCHAIN '/opt/moe/toolchain' is where the 'toolchain' mode installs Node, and only a check job puts it first (:1434).
- agent-seat.mjs installs the pinned toolchain at seat-start.
So the toolchain is in the seat VM but off the agent's PATH. A verified-local worker can never run the plan's local verification (TDD red/green, npm test), and QA can't re-run anything either.

Plan this so that agent jobs can run the project's Node toolchain, or, if that is deliberately excluded, say so and make planning and worker guidance consistent with it (verification only through requiredChecks in check VMs). Questions to settle:
- whether npm ci with registry dependencies works in the seat VM, given its egress;
- whether QA jobs need the same.
NOTE: changing guest-supervisor.py moves its pinned sha256 (CERTIFICATION_PINS.supervisorSha256 616463b7…, packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/certificationEvidence.ts:28). That means updating the pin and the CERTIFICATION.md table, then re-certifying BOTH hosts in a governor-run certify (about 15 min each). Both certify runs passed on 11-05 with the current pin.
1a8f1d0e's DoD 8 Windows run is re-run once this lands.
definitionOfDone: Inside a verified-local worker or QA job, `node` and `npm` resolve to the pinned toolchain (or the plan documents and tests a deliberate alternative), so a plan's local `npm test` runs in the seat VM. Covered by the guest-supervisor tests of the agent job env.
The plan states what the agent job can install (npm ci against the registry under the seat VM's egress) and pins it with a test or a recorded real-VM line.

If guest-supervisor.py changes: CERTIFICATION_PINS.supervisorSha256 and the CERTIFICATION.md table carry the new sha, readiness accepts only the new pin, and the governor records a passing re-certify on Windows and on Linux (WSL).
docs/roles/architect.reference.md (Verified-local plans) and the worker guidance say what a verified-local job can run locally, consistent with the code.
A governor real-VM re-run of the Windows DoD 8 task gets past local verification: the worker completes its steps and calls complete_task.

- An untracked `node_modules` directory never leaves the VM. Any other file a command writes into the workspace does: a worker's lands with the change, and a QA job that leaves one is refused. So delete build, coverage and report output before finishing, or write it under `$HOME` or `/tmp`.
- Local runs are the seat's own evidence. Delivery comes only from the approved required checks in check VMs.

Leave docs/roles/architect.md and worker.md alone (40-line cap). Test: checkRefs[1] asserts these sentinels and runs the role-doc lint.

Correction to step 2, item (6) of this plan (architect-3669a6f6, plan rev 1). Item (6) names `moe.unblock_worker {taskId, resolveBlocks: true}`. That call cannot unpark this row. unblock_worker requires workerId and resolution and takes no taskId, and resolveBlocks only restores BLOCKED rows the named worker still holds. Step 2's park frees the seat, so no worker holds this row.

The unpark is `moe.set_task_status {taskId, status: "WORKING", reason}`, and the governor has said they will do it. Pass a reason that states only settled facts, for example "R-win, R-wsl, R-dod8 and R-npm are posted on this row as comments <ids>; step 2's wait is met." With blockedOnTaskIds [] and no resource lease, an unpark without a reason carries the block text forward as an "UNANSWERED BLOCK … OPEN question … re-block" reopenReason (carriedBlockQuestion, packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts:139). The resuming worker would then re-block on records that are already posted. The move is not a reopen (blockedFromStatus is WORKING), so finished steps stay COMPLETED.

Workers: nothing else changes. Step 2's items (1)–(5) and its park via report_blocked stand as written.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Guidance only, calling /opt/moe/toolchain/bin/node by absolute path: rejected. npm's `#!/usr/bin/env node` still exits 127 without node on PATH, and npm scripts spawn bare `node`.
- PATH only, with a copy-the-workspace workflow for installs: rejected. Every verified-local plan and every QA re-run would need a copy prelude. An in-place npm ci would still poison the candidate: node_modules/.bin symlinks are refused as SNAPSHOT_SYMLINK_DENIED, the 10,000-entry cap gives SNAPSHOT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, and any byte refuses QA. Adding the export skip later would cost a second supervisor move and a second re-certify of both hosts. So the node_modules skip ships in the same supervisor change.
- One row for code, docs and records: about 10 files, which is the hard cap. And the CERTIFICATION.md table can only record reports of the LANDED supervisor. So the code moved to prerequisite task-ccbff5c6 (5 files, HIGH, planned by its own architect), and this row keeps the docs, the generated initFiles.ts, the certification record and the governor's runs, behind dependsOn (mem split-dod-via-prerequisites pattern).
- Export honoring .gitignore: rejected. That is a new parser inside the security boundary, and node_modules is the one tree an install writes and the one that holds symlinks.
- Registry reachability as a unit test: not possible without network and a VM. Unit tests pin what the code controls (PATH, no netns, the skip), and the governor's real-VM probe pins the egress itself (DoD 2 allows 'a test or a recorded real-VM line').
- A scope check against the working tree in the gate: dropped. The control checkout where QA re-runs carries foreign dirt (package-lock.json files, build.gradle.kts), so the check would fail there; QA checks scope with git show --stat of the completion.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
What a verified-local agent job can install, once task-ccbff5c6 lands:
- `npm ci` and `npm install` run in place from registry.npmjs.org. The bridge job has no network namespace (only check_job passes netns), so it uses the seat VM's NAT egress, the same route the agent CLI's own API calls take. certify's guest-network check proves only the VM gateway's daemon ports are closed to it.
- Its node_modules output never reaches the candidate.
- QA jobs go through the same start_job (the role only picks the prompt and MOE_ROLE), so they get the same PATH. The skip keeps their candidate empty after an in-place npm ci.

Check jobs stay offline: GUARD's empty netns plus the approved offline dependency tree.

Other facts:
- The agent could already exec /opt/moe/toolchain/bin/node by absolute path (root-owned, readable; the writer-containment certify check), so the PATH change grants no new capability.
- The materialized workspace holds no .git or other CONTROL_SEGMENTS (source-snapshot.mjs:22).
- Changing guest-supervisor.py moves the check environment id too (check-evidence.mjs checkEnvironment), so the scratch project's checkEnvironments needs the new id at its first landing.
